label: late original-phase u/q/2/t/p/z input in sequences starting with i/x/m/d/l
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at t<3, on <DEL>, or during copying. Rate rises with position (orig_idx 3 -> 8 goes 0.8% -> 9%), and it fires most on the last few inputs before <DEL> (to_go 0-2). The current input matters: u (7x lift), q, 2, t, then p, z, j, g; mostly the first time that token appears. The sequence context matters too: rate is 3-5x higher when the first original token is i, x, m, d or l. The strongest activations are on a final u/q/z in sequences starting with i/d/x. The conjunction predicate gets dev F1 0.49 (precision 0.62, recall 0.41, mass recall 0.54). Missed activations are weak firings on other tokens or in other contexts (e.g. sequences starting with s or a), which suggests a distributed hidden-state code rather than a clean rule. Magnitude grows with position and with the strong-token/strong-prefix combination.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: u, q, 2, t, p, z; least: a, y, l, i) and the first original token (most: i, x, m, d, l, r; least: p, t, q, u); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, L=9 & t=8.
